alerts.headline: From 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., Tuesday, Sept. 22, expect several closures of SR 109 lasting up to 45 minutes each. Crews will deliver and install five support beams on the new bridge. Read more about this fish barrier removal work on the project webpage.
Overnight southbound I-5 lane and ramp closures resume the week of Sept. 28 between Maytown Rd and Old Hwy 99 for a paving project.

Expect around-the-clock single-lane alternating traffic on US 101 at the Jefferson-Clallam county line. The speed limit is reduced to 25 mph between mileposts 184 and 185. Crews are building a bridge to improve fish passage in May Creek.

Expect lane reductions overnight in southbound lanes of I-5 until 9:30 a.m. Saturday, Oct. 3 for concrete panel replacement. Starting Tuesday, Oct. 6, crews will work in northbound lanes nightly until 9 a.m. Saturday, Oct. 10. If it rains, work may be rescheduled.

Monday, Sept. 14 through Monday, Oct. 12: Travelers in both directions of SR 6 will take turns moving through a single lane between Clinton Road (milepost 45.6) and Twin Oaks Road (milepost 46.5), weekdays from 7 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., for work to replace a buried water main line. Flaggers will direct travelers through the work zone. Plan ahead and expect delays. This work is being done by Boistfort Valley Water Corporation.

Thursday, Oct. 1 to Thursday, Oct. 29: Travelers in both directions of SR 6, between mileposts 32 and 35.6, will take turns moving through a single-lane weekdays, from 7 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., for tree trimming around power lines. Flaggers will direct travelers through the area. Plan ahead and expect delays.

Road work on US 101 both directions from milepost 97.43 near Failor Lk Rd to milepost 99.6 near Hoquiam River beginning at 6:35 am on October 2, 2026 until about 8:00 pm. Motorists can expect up to 30-minutes of delay through the area.

Expect temporary traffic lights and single-lane alternating traffic around the clock on US 101 near Ruby Beach. The speed limit is reduced from 55 mph to 25 mph from milepost 162.93 to 163.51. Work is for a fish passage project.

Travelers will need to prepare for around-the-clock closures at the US 101 Hoh River Bridge. From 5 a.m. Thursday, Oct. 1 to noon Tuesday, Oct. 6, the US 101 Hoh River Bridge will close to all traffic for emergency repairs.
Reduced speeds and one-way alternating traffic controlled by a signal is in place until further notice on US 101 near Cedar Creek at milepost 165.

Closure on US 101 in both directions at milepost 177, across the Hoh River Bridge beginning at 5:00 am on October 1, 2026 until about 12:00 pm on October 6, 2026.  Road is closed. There are no detours available.
Road work on SR 8 westbound at milepost 17.56 near Wilson Rd NW beginning at 9:14 am on October 2, 2026 until about 3:00 pm.
Expect temporary traffic lights and single-lane alternating traffic on SR 109 at milepost 37 near Taholah. The speed limit is reduced from 50 mph to 25 mph. Read more on the project webpage.
Road work on US 101 both directions at milepost 189 near Mansfield Rd beginning at 11:39 am on September 9, 2026 until further notice.
Expect around-the-clock single-lane alternating traffic approaching milepost 184 near Dowans Creek Road. The road is reduced to one lane until permanent repairs are completed due to a slide.
The climbing lane on northbound US 101 approaching Cosi Hill is closed.

Expect temporary traffic lights and single-lane alternating traffic around the clock through fall on SR 109 near Moclips Highway. The speed limit is reduced from 50 mph to 25 mph. Read more on the project webpage.

Expect temporary traffic lights and single-lane alternating traffic around the clock through fall on SR 109 at milepost 33.8 north of Moclips. The speed limit is reduced from 50 mph to 25 mph. Read more on the project webpage.
Road work on US 101 northbound from milepost 359.58 near Schneider Creek to milepost 350 near SR 3 beginning at 8:02 am on October 2, 2026 until about 1:00 pm.
